about.title: Woodside Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Woodside's mix of rural estate properties, landscaping crews, equestrian facilities, and small commercial operations along corridors like Woodside Road and Portola Road means workplace injuries here often don't look like a typical office slip-and-fall. Someone might be hurt using a contractor's ladder, injured by a defective piece of equipment on a job site, or struck by another vehicle while making a delivery near Rt 84. In California, workers' compensation is generally your only path against your own employer, no matter who was at fault. But when a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to the accident, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free connection service that puts injured workers in touch with an independent attorney who can look at the details of a Woodside workplace incident and explain what avenues might apply.

whyChoose.title: Why People in Woodside Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Workers' Comp vs. Third-Party Claims
items.desc: An independent attorney can help you understand that while workers' comp is usually your exclusive remedy against your employer, a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — may still be liable separately.

items.title: Knowing Your Reporting Deadlines
items.desc: California requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim, so getting guidance early matters.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury, and an attorney can help you understand your rights if you're worried about your job.

items.question: I was hurt doing landscaping work on a Woodside property — can I still file a claim if I'm not a direct employee?
items.answer: It depends on your working relationship with the property owner or contractor. If you were an independent contractor rather than an employee, workers' comp may not apply, but a third-party negligence claim against a property owner or equipment supplier could be worth exploring. An independent attorney can review the facts of your situation and explain what applies.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work along Woodside Road or Rt 84?
items.answer: If another driver caused the crash while you were performing work duties, you may have both a workers' compensation claim and a separate third-party claim against that driver. These two paths can sometimes run alongside each other. An attorney can help sort out how they interact in your specific case.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim if a third party caused my workplace injury?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of the injury. Workers' compensation reporting deadlines are separate and much shorter, so it's worth reporting to your employer within 30 days regardless. Talking to an attorney early can help you avoid missing either deadline.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm that will represent me?
items.answer: No — LawProactive is a free service that connects injured workers with independent attorneys in our network. We don't provide legal representation ourselves, and any attorney you're connected with typically works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
